title: Federated Free Storage Mesh - object manifest record
description: What the mesh knows about one stored object: its content hash, its size, which privacy and criticality class it belongs to, which backend holds it, which backends hold replicas, and where it sits in the compaction lifecycle. What the object *contains* is deliberately not representable here, and neither is any key that would open it. The row is a closed field set in the manner of experience_ledger.schema.json: an unknown field is rejected rather than stored, so a caller that forgot to strip a bearer token cannot smuggle one in under a new name. The closed set alone is not enough - a field typed merely 'string' is a slot that will hold an API key as happily as it holds a mime type - so every string here is typed as what it actually is (a digest, a classifier, a provider id, a key reference, a timestamp) and bounded by pattern and maxLength, every array by maxItems. Two privacy rules are encoded as structure rather than as prose, because prose is not a control: a LOCAL_ONLY object can only name a local backend, and a CONFIDENTIAL object on an external backend must carry client-side encryption metadata. This schema declares encryption fields; it does not define or implement the encryption contract. Backend identity is the one thing this schema cannot settle alone. primary_backend and replica_backends are enumerated against the provider registry, so a backend nobody registered is an invalid document; but whether a registered row was actually *admitted* - verified free, healthy, writable, permitted for this privacy class, tier and size - is runtime state no JSON Schema can read. AI_SKILL_LIBRARY/v4/storage/mesh_validator.py resolves that half. Passing this schema is therefore necessary and not sufficient: a placement is admissible only when both halves agree.

authority.description: Spec S7: a manifest record is evidence about an object, never authority over one.

object_id.description: A content-derived opaque id, never a name. Spec S7 requires that object names carry no secrets and no unnecessary private text; a digest is the only shape that cannot. 'users/alice/tax-return-2025.pdf' is rejected by construction, not by review.

object_class.description: What kind of thing this is - 'benchmark-bundle', 'replay', 'checkpoint'. A classifier from a small controlled vocabulary, so the mesh can reason about categories without any field ever holding a filename or a description.

mime_type.description: Type and subtype only. RFC 2045 parameters are excluded because 'name=' and 'filename=' are exactly the private text S7 forbids in object naming.

replica_backends.description: Full replicas, not stripes (Spec S9). Bounded: an object needing more than eight independent copies is a policy question, not a manifest question.

lifecycle_state.description: The compaction lifecycle of Spec S12. These are the mesh's own object states; they name no runtime, residency or governance state belonging to another plane.

allOf.title: LOCAL_ONLY never leaves owned/local storage
allOf.description: Spec S4. Encoded as structure: for a LOCAL_ONLY object the only values the backend fields will accept are local backend ids, so a manifest naming an external provider is not a policy violation to be detected later - it is an invalid document.

allOf.title: CONFIDENTIAL reaches an external backend only as ciphertext
allOf.description: Spec S4/S21. Either the object never leaves a local backend, or it is client-side encrypted and carries the encryption metadata that proves it - algorithm, scheme version and a key *reference*. The encryption flag alone is not accepted, because a flag is an assertion and the metadata is the evidence.

allOf.title: CANONICAL and METADATA carry no bulk object data
allOf.description: Spec S6 and policy.yaml tiers.*.bulk_object_data_allowed. CANONICAL's primary home is GitHub and METADATA's is the object index; both hold pointers, not payloads. Until now that was a sentence in policy.yaml and nothing else, so a manifest could declare storage_tier CANONICAL with size_bytes of one tebibyte and be accepted. The bound is the same 1 MiB the provider schema already applies to the metadata service, so the two cannot drift.

allOf.title: Supabase is metadata and index only, keyed on identity
allOf.description: Spec S6/S18/S25. The provider schema confines Supabase through adapter_type, which a row can decline to wear by relabelling itself s3_compatible; that schema now pins the adapter to the identity, and this rule pins the manifest side to the same identity. Naming supabase as primary or as a replica forces the METADATA tier and the bounded size with it, so the confinement holds at the surface that decides where a byte actually lands rather than only at admission time.

allOf.title: encryption_state NONE carries no encryption metadata
allOf.description: The flag and its evidence could contradict each other: a manifest declaring encryption_state NONE was accepted with a fully populated encryption block, algorithm, scheme version and key reference included. That is a record saying at once that the object is plaintext and that a key opens it, and whichever half a later reader trusts, the other is a lie. Neither is a safe default to guess, so the document is refused instead.

allOf.title: CLIENT_SIDE_ENCRYPTED carries its encryption metadata
allOf.description: The converse, and the reason it was missed: the CONFIDENTIAL rule already demanded the metadata, so a CONFIDENTIAL object could not claim encryption without evidence - but a PUBLIC or INTERNAL object could, and an unverifiable encryption claim on an object nobody double-checks is exactly how a plaintext object comes to be treated as ciphertext. The claim now costs the same evidence in every class.

class_token.description: A classifier drawn from a small controlled vocabulary - 'replay-bundle', 'evidence.compacted'. Lower-case, punctuation-limited and short, because a classifier that can hold a sentence can hold a prompt, and one that can hold 2KB can hold a credential. Two bounds are load-bearing rather than tidy. maxLength is 40: a 256-bit key is 64 characters as hex and 44 as base64, so neither shape fits, and a review found a 64-character hex private key accepted as an object_class. The 'not' clause refuses a token that is nothing but hex from sixteen characters up, which closes the shorter hex forms that would still fit; below that a pure-hex token is a plausible classifier and too small to be key material. The lower-case pattern already excludes base64 and upper-case base32. A classifier this field cannot express is a sign the vocabulary needs a considered entry, not a longer field.

sha256.description: Lower-case hex digest. Fixed length, so the field cannot double as a payload slot.

backend_id.description: A backend id is not free text and not merely a well-shaped token: it is a key into the provider registry, so the values accepted here are exactly the provider_ids checked into AI_SKILL_LIBRARY/v4/storage/providers.yaml. A pattern alone let 'some_random_untrusted_host' through, because a pattern describes a shape and the question here is identity. The enum is the half of that question a JSON Schema can answer - registry membership is a fact checked into the repository. The other half, whether that row is *admitted* (verified free, healthy, writable, permitted for this privacy class and tier), is runtime state a schema cannot see; it is enforced by AI_SKILL_LIBRARY/v4/storage/mesh_validator.py, and a manifest is only placed when both agree. Registry membership is not admission.

local_backend_id.description: An owned/local store. The 'local_' prefix is reserved: storage_provider.schema.json forbids any external provider from claiming a provider_id that starts with it, which is what makes the LOCAL_ONLY rule above airtight rather than merely conventional. Like backend_id this is also enumerated against the registry, so the 'local_' namespace reservation cannot be satisfied by a local-looking name that no owned store answers to.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 / RFC 3339 instant, enforced by pattern. 'format: date-time' is an annotation a validator is free to ignore, and the default one does.

evidence_ref.description: A pointer into the existing verifier/evidence path, not a note about one and not a way to fetch one. Either a scheme-qualified reference or a repository-relative path whose final segment carries a file extension, so that the placeholders which satisfy a mere minLength - '   ', 'n/a', 'TODO' - do not satisfy an evidence requirement. The character set is the control. It previously admitted 222 characters including ? # & = % @, which is not the shape of a pointer - it is the shape of a presigned URL ('?X-Amz-Credential=...&X-Amz-Signature=...'), a token callback ('?token=...') and a basic-auth URL ('//user:pass@host'), all of which a review got accepted here. Query strings, fragments and userinfo are gone, because an evidence reference that carries its own authorisation is a credential stored in a manifest.

provenance.description: Where the object came from, as classifiers and references. Not prose: a free-text origin note is where 'exported from the user's inbox at their request' - and the next thing after it - gets written down.

encryption_metadata.description: Spec S21: algorithm, version and a key *reference* only. There is deliberately no field a plaintext key could be written into - additionalProperties is false, so 'key', 'key_material', 'dek' and 'passphrase' are rejected outright - and the fields that do exist are shaped so they cannot be repurposed as one. key_ref must be a scheme-qualified pointer at a secret store, and the schemes it accepts are exactly the key locations Spec S22 allows; an object-storage URL is not among them, which is how key/ciphertext separation is enforced structurally. nonce and tag are capped at 32 characters: long enough for a 12-byte nonce and a 16-byte authentication tag, too short to hold a 256-bit key (44 base64 characters). This schema names these fields; it does not define the encryption contract or implement any cryptography.

algorithm.description: The AEAD construction the ciphertext was produced with, as a closed vocabulary drawn from policy.yaml encryption.allowed_algorithms. It was a class_token, which made the one field sitting next to key_ref exactly wide enough for a raw hex private key. Spec S21 requires a well-supported standard library approach rather than invented cryptography, so these are the standard authenticated constructions such a library offers. This schema names the algorithm; it neither chooses nor implements one.

key_ref.description: A pointer to where the key lives, never the key. Schemes limited to the secret locations Spec S22 permits, so a reference into the same bucket as the ciphertext, or a bare hex blob that happens to be the key itself, is rejected.

authority_flags.description: Denied by name rather than by omission. The scalar authority:false above is the canonical declaration; these name the specific authorities a storage record does not hold, so a later document cannot acquire one by adding a key.
